info.bio:
Screamin' Jay Hawkins (nacido como Jalacy Hawkins) fue un popular cantante afroamericano oriundo de Cleveland, Ohio, y que obtuvo éxito durante la explosión del rock a mediados de los años cincuenta. Conocido por sus circenses actuaciones y estética en ocasiones macabra, grabó uno de los mayores éxitos del momento, I put a spell on you en 1957.

Pese a que en un principio, Hawkins quiso dedicarse a la ópera, esta ambición terminó por desaparecer y viró su carrera hacia el blues y la interpretación del piano.

scenes.name: Rock'n'roll
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Fusión de rhythm'n'blues y country, con mucho más peso del primero. Chuck Berry inventa en 1955 el rock'n'roll tal como se conocerá durante cincuenta años (la guitarra como instrumento protagonista, canciones propias que hablan a los adolescentes); Bo Diddley aporta el ritmo «hambone», Little Richard y Esquerita el histerismo y el maquillaje (el primer «decadence-rock»), Jerry Lee Lewis el piano feroz y Sun Records el rockabilly. Elvis Presley es, para Scaruffi, «la primera gran estafa del rock'n'roll». Buddy Holly y Eddie Cochran abren otra vía; en paralelo nacen el soul (Ray Charles), la exótica (Martin Denny, Esquivel), la música electrónica de cinta y, en Gran Bretaña, el skiffle.

podcast.title: Classical Music Background
podcast.body: Prior to his rock and roll career, Screamin' Jay Hawkins studied classical music. "adopted by a tribe of blackfoot Indians and studied classical music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emerging from a Coffin
podcast.body: Famous DJ Alan Fried offered Screamin' Jay Hawkins $300 to perform "I Put a Spell on You" live, with the condition that Hawkins emerge from a coffin. Hawkins accepted and continued this macabre act. "The only catch was that Hawkins had to emerge from a coffin to sing the song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Macabre Stage Display
podcast.body: His live shows were characterized by crazy clothes, props like snakes and a skull, smoke bombs, and incantations, where he screamed and grunted, incorporating elements of death, voodoo, and black magic to freak out audiences. "Jay screamed and grunted his way to fame, freaking out people along the way with his macabre display of death and voodoo and black magic and whatever else."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-War Career Start
podcast.body: After serving in the army during World War II, Screamin' Jay Hawkins became a singer known for his very theatrical performances. "When he got out of the army after World War II, he became a singer, a very, very theatrical singer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Scandalous Stage Presence
podcast.body: Screaming Jay Hawkins captivated audiences with his possessed singing style and highly theatrical, scandalous stage performances. He often appeared in a coffin, and incorporated props like skulls and fire, which deeply shocked and scandalized audiences of his time. "Screaming y Hawking cantaba como un poseso, aparecían a taude, sus abacalabedas, fuego y elementos que escandalizaron a la audiencia."

srcs.episode: El punk existía antes de Sex Pistols (y era algo salvaje)

podcast.title: Skull Prop "Henry"
podcast.body: As part of his theatrical performances, Screamin' Jay Hawkins used props including a skull on top of a walking stick, which he named Henry. "He had a skull on the top of a walking stick and the skull's name was Henry, by the way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
